profile.name: Dr. Neelesh Rao
profile.bio: I design systems that make invisible engineering ideas visible. My work sits at the intersection of embedded intelligence, energy-aware computation, and engineering education.
profile.longBio: Dr. Neelesh Rao is a professor and systems researcher working across embedded intelligence, cyber-physical systems, and engineering pedagogy. His lab builds compact, explainable prototypes that move from a lecture diagram to a working bench experiment.
profile.availability: Open to research collaborations and doctoral supervision.

researchAreas.title: Embedded intelligence
researchAreas.summary: Low-power systems that sense, decide, and respond at the edge.
researchAreas.detail: TinyML, sensor fusion, real-time systems, and dependable firmware for constrained environments.

researchAreas.title: Energy-aware computing
researchAreas.summary: Engineering computation around the physical limits of energy.
researchAreas.detail: Power profiling, adaptive control, and hardware-software co-design for resilient devices.

researchAreas.title: Engineering education
researchAreas.summary: Interactive models that make difficult systems easier to reason about.
researchAreas.detail: Simulation-led learning, visual explanations, and classroom instruments for systems thinking.

featuredProjects.title: HarborSense: edge analytics for coastal monitoring
featuredProjects.summary: A battery-aware sensor node that turns noisy shoreline measurements into a clear signal for local operators.

featuredProjects.title: Motor control, made inspectable
featuredProjects.summary: A visual lab kit that lets students see the relationship between duty cycle, torque, and thermal load.
